# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 34 (Bi-Vb Pc34)
**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc34
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 34
**Title (English, from literature):** Not nursing a disciple
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-pc34
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 34, titled *Naupaṭṭhāpana* ("Not nursing a disciple"), establishes that a nun who fails to nurse or attend upon a sick monastic disciple incurs an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. As analyzed by Ute Hüsken, while reciprocal duties to nurse a sick co-resident or pupil throughout their illness also appear for monks (such as in Mahāvagga 1.33), neglect of this duty is nowhere classified as an offense for monks, whereas for nuns it is formally penalised as a Pātimokkha rule [Hüsken 1997]. The rule's casuistry further specifies that an *ācarinī* (teacher) who fails to tend to an ill *antevāsī* (pupil) incurs a lesser *dukkaṭa* (wrongdoing) offense [Hüsken 1997]. The non-offense section (*anāpatti*) exempts the nun if external obstacles prevent her, if she is unable despite making efforts, if she herself is ill, or in the case of unforeseen accidents [Hüsken 1997].
SuttaCentral records extensive canonical parallels across early Buddhist monastic traditions, including the Theravāda Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bi-pm-pc34*) and Bhikkhunī Parivāra, Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Pc 93*), Mahīśāsaka (*Lzh Mi Bi Vb Pc 123*), Sarvāstivāda (*Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Pc 102*), and Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinayas in both Chinese (*Lzh Mu Bi Vb Pc 99*) and Tibetan (*xct-mu-bi-vb-pc93*) [SuttaCentral]. In algorithmic text-reuse analysis, DharmaNexus identifies 282 matching segments across 60 Pali texts, with the most extensive shared formulaic passages found in other Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules including Pācittiya 78, 77, 70, 68, 23, and 33 [DharmaNexus]. The rule has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
